label: PF Backlog 680
title: Event dispatcher remediation: backoff, concurrency, cursor recovery, metrics and DLQ ownership
body: Fix accepted 1269 implementation findings: real DispatchOnce tests, backoff/status filtering, concurrency claim, cursor recovery after failed rows, filter semantics, cross-tenant collision errors, created_at retention, per-event failure isolation, dispatcher metrics/logs, registry registration, and an explicit DLQ ownership decision.

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=32056205cd98
BLOCKER:
  - AC-3 requires "store registry evidence is present"; neither spec_pack nor design_pack references any store registry artifact/entry — only migration and test files — so AC-3 is unmet as designed.
  - AC-3 requires "migration rollback requires a verified backup"; rollout/rollback only say "with backup" with no verified backup/restore step, evidence, or restore test — data-loss exposure on 0026 down (guardrail 1).
MAJOR:
  - C-1/C-2 set `tenant_test: 'N/A: tenant RLS migration'` while AC-2 requires rejecting cross-tenant collisions; runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS) and tenant binding are never proven (CL-011, guardrail 3).
  - C-5 uses `migrations/0025_...up.sql` as its own positive/negative/tenant "test" with evidence "migration applied locally" — not a fail-able test; AC-3's testability requirement is unsatisfied.
  - observability_runbook is APPLICABLE but cites only a design doc and a unit test; no runbook artifact, alert ownership, probe backoff/cooldown, or dependency-down behavior (CL-014, guardrail 2 SPOF/alert lead-time).
  - Guardrail 6: migration-interrupted/partial-apply recovery and rollback verification are not specified; "Revert the change" is not an operable rollback procedure.
  - `affected_files`, `affected_components`, `risks` are "Not specified" while controls reference concrete files — declared scope and traceability are incomplete for gate review.
MINOR:
  - FR-1/2/3 all map to the same single test file and design doc; per-AC evidence granularity is too coarse for independent verification.
  - `config_contract` is `{'N/A': 'reuse dispatcher options'}` without naming the reused options — drift risk against guardrail 10 reuse.
  - `nfr_slo` marked N/A while `nfr: bounded batch` imposes a performance bound with no stated value or measurement.
NIT:
  - `stop_conditions: ['transport implementation']` and `out_of_scope: ['Not specified.']` are ambiguous/placeholder phrasing.
  - `rollback: Revert the change` duplicates but conflicts in specificity with the design's "run 0026 down with backup" — consolidate to one authoritative statement.
SUMMARY:
  - Design covers backoff, DLQ, concurrency tests and metrics directionally, but AC-3 fails on two counts: no store-registry evidence and no verified backup/restore path for 0026.
  - Top risks: tenant-collision controls ship without tenant/role tests (CL-011), C-5's "test" is a migration file, and no ops runbook/alert ownership exists for dispatcher/worker/DB failure.
  - Gate should not pass until registry evidence, verified backup procedure, runtime role posture proof, and a real runbook artifact are added.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=d082f6deed5a
BLOCKER:
  - AC-1 unmet: no fail-able tests for retry-with-backoff/status gating, cursor recovery (stale 'processing' reclaim), or concurrent passes; only matching/dedupe/DLQ exist.
  - DLQ coverage is solely in a `PF_DB_DSN`-gated test that skips by default, so it is not fail-able in CI; traceability claims all three ACs to this one skipping file.
  - AC-3 evidence absent from diff: no store-registry/ownership record and no ADR-0012 reuse/amendment shown for event delivery/DLQ ownership.
MAJOR:
  - AC-2 requires "metrics/logs": diff emits metrics only; no log lines for delivery failure, DLQ, stale reclaim, or cross-tenant collision.
  - Failure isolation gap: a backing-off or non-stale 'processing' head event does `return st, nil`, halting the entire pass — head-of-line blocking up to StaleAfter (5m default) starves all later events.
  - Cross-tenant collision rejection (control C-2) ships with no positive/negative test in `event_dispatcher_test.go`; `UpsertSubscription` `n==0` path is untested.
  - Verified-backup requirement for 0026 rollback is only a SQL comment; no documented/verified backup-restore procedure accompanies the destructive down migration.
MINOR:
  - Deploy ordering risk: `beginDelivery` INSERT now references `created_at`; code-live-before-0026 (or 0026 rollback while code deployed) breaks every dispatch pass.
  - `event_subscriptions.go` adds `fmt.Errorf` with no import hunk in the diff — verify the package builds.
  - Confirm `EventStore.metrics` defaults to `nopEventMetrics` (or all constructors call `WithMetrics`); four new call sites in `DispatchOnce` panic if nil.
  - `matchesFilter` uses `fmt.Sprint` coercion (`"1"` matches numeric `1`) and re-parses JSON per subscription per event; no test for type-coercion/nested-key semantics.
  - Reclaimed/stale and DLQ'd-then-advanced rows are all counted/emitted as `DeliverySkipped`, muddying observability.
NIT:
  - `StaleAfter` is an undocumented knob (no comment on semantics/ops tuning) alongside `MaxAttempts`/`BaseBackoff`.
  - `actionAdvance` on `failed` status increments `Skipped` rather than a distinct dedupe counter.
SUMMARY:
  - Behavior changes (state gating, atomic cursor+delivery, cross-tenant error) are directionally right, but AC-1 test coverage and AC-3 evidence are objectively missing, and AC-2's "logs" half is unimplemented.
  - Top risks: skipping integration test masks DLQ proof in CI; pass-halting on retry/stale rows threatens availability; missing backup procedure for a destructive rollback.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
